parameters {

}

model {

}

generated_quantities {
  real nu;
  nu ~ normal_rng(mu, 1);
}

And have all of the distributions in Stan been rng'd, or are there still a few exceptions?

messages.author: 839dfa09184985a5
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Forward Sampling Examples
parts:
On 8/1/13 11:58 AM, Michael Betancourt wrote:
I'm referring to generating random quantities in the "generated quantities" block, a la posterior predictive checking.  In other words is this the general procedure?

I believe so. There are a few examples with simple models in src/models/ARM/Ch.3 and src/models/ARM/Ch.4 in the feature/ARM branch like https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/blob/feature/ARM/src/models/ARM/Ch.3/kidiq_prediction.stan.

parameters {
  real mu;
}

model {
  mu ~ normal(0, 1);
}

generated_quantities {
  real nu;
  nu ~ normal_rng(mu, 1);
}

And have all of the distributions in Stan been rng'd, or are there still a few exceptions?

I believe that most of the distributions support rng, but some extensions of distributions such as bernoullie_logit do not support rngs. Below is a more conclusive list (from test/gm/model_specs/compiled/rng.stan) where // indicates that the rng is not yet supported.

  n <- bernoulli_rng(0.5);
  // n <- bernoulli_logit_rng(0.0);
  n <- binomial_rng(15,0.3);
  // n <- binomial_logit_rng(15,-1.2);
  n <- beta_binomial_rng(42, 0.3, 1.9);
  n <- hypergeometric_rng(5,4,9);
  n <- neg_binomial_rng(1.2,3.9);
  n <- ordered_logistic_rng(1.9,theta);
  n <- poisson_rng(2.7);
  // n <- poisson_log_rng(2.7);

  n <- categorical_rng(theta);
  ns <- multinomial_rng(theta,20);

  z <- normal_rng(0,1);
  z <- exp_mod_normal_rng(0.2,1.9,1.5);
  z <- skew_normal_rng(1.1, 2.3, 9.8);
  z <- student_t_rng(3,1,2);
  z <- cauchy_rng(-1.0,2.9);
  z <- double_exponential_rng(1.0,3.8);
  z <- logistic_rng(1.0,3.8);
  z <- gumbel_rng(-1.0,2.31);
  z <- lognormal_rng(-1.0, 3.6);
  z <- chi_square_rng(4.1);
  z <- inv_chi_square_rng(4.1);
  z <- scaled_inv_chi_square_rng(1.0, 3.0);
  z <- exponential_rng(2.9);
  z <- gamma_rng(1.0, 3.0);
  z <- inv_gamma_rng(0.1,0.1);
  z <- weibull_rng(1.0,2.0);
  z <- pareto_rng(0.1, 1.5);
  z <- beta_rng(110.0, 250.1);
  z <- uniform_rng(-1.0, 1.0);
  z <- rayleigh_rng(1.0); 
 
  theta <- dirichlet_rng(alpha);
  v <- multi_normal_rng(mu,Sigma);
  // v <- multi_normal_prec_rng(mu,Sigma);
  // v <- multi_normal_cholesky_rng(mu,L);
  v <- multi_student_t_rng(3.0,mu,Sigma);
  Sigma <- wishart_rng(3.0,Sigma);
  Sigma <- inv_wishart_rng(3.0,Sigma);
  Sigma <- lkj_corr_rng(3,2.5);
  L <- lkj_corr_cholesky_rng(3,3.0);
  // DEPRECATE:  Sigma <- lkj_cov_rng(Sigma, mu, alpha, 2.0);

I'm not sure what you mean by forward sampling, but the ARM models that I've added are all in the branch feature/arm. Peter
